summary: Executed targeted regression tests for workspace import validation/merge logic and mocked Settings UI import flow. Found one critical merge conflict misclassification edge case and one mobile design issue.

critical.issue: False conflict detected when existing DB-normalized optional arrays are [] but incoming record omits those optional fields (example: prompts.linked* arrays). Re-import of semantically identical data can be flagged as conflict.

ui_bugs.issue: At 390px width, fixed left navigation leaves very narrow content column; import controls/guidance become cramped and hard to read.

integration_issues.issue: Console shows a 502 resource error in preview run. Page still rendered with test intercepts, but failing request should be traced.

issues: Poor readable width for labels and import guidance
Primary content appears squeezed by persistent sidebar

action_items: Normalize optional default-like fields during canonical comparison (e.g., treat missing optional arrays equivalent to empty arrays where schema semantics imply defaults) to avoid false conflicts on re-import.
Investigate the preview 502 request surfaced during Settings load and ensure graceful handling.
Improve small-screen Settings layout so import controls remain readable/usable at 390px width.
critical_code_review_comments: mergeWorkspaceImport canonical comparison is strict for [] vs undefined; this breaks expected idempotent re-import behavior for older/normalized exports.
Many interactive controls in settings route still lack data-testid attributes, reducing UI regression testability and violating the stated testability convention.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run /app/tests/workspace_import_review.test.ts first (18/18 pass). Then confirm fix for optional-array false conflict by re-running /app/tests/workspace_import_conflict_probe.ts; current output shows prompts conflict for semantically identical data.
rca of the issue: RCA: canonical() removes undefined object fields but keeps explicit empty arrays, so previous row with normalized [] and incoming row with omitted optional field are considered different. Reproduction: run /app/tests/workspace_import_conflict_probe.ts; expected unchanged/no conflicts, actual includes prompts conflict. Mitigation: canonical normalization layer for optional defaults before compare (or collection-aware compare that maps omitted optional arrays to []).
